A deduction is a conclusion based on clues. must be = very sure. might / could be = possible. can't be = very sure it is not true. Past deductions use have + past participle. Use It seems that... and It's very likely that... to introduce a problem.

I can explain the difference between must, might and can't. I use can't, not mustn't, for negative deductions. I can form past deductions with have + past participle. I can introduce a problem with It seems that.... I can troubleshoot a problem aloud with three deductions.
Predict future events at work and show how sure you are, using will, adverbs like definitely and probably, and the modals may / might / could.

A prediction is what you think will happen. Your words show how certain you are. Certainty scale 100% will surely / will definitely + base verb 80% will probably + base verb 50% may / might / could + base verb 0% will not / won't + base verb

He will surely finish the report today. She will definitely join the call. It will not work without the update. The client won't definitely agree. (not sure they will agree) Word order with adverbs With will, the adverb goes after will in positive sentences: will definitely, will probably. In negative sentences, it goes before won't: definitely won't, probably won't.

I think he can finish it by Friday. The release may slip to next week. The team might need more time. It could be a good opportunity. She will probably send the budget tomorrow. Modals use the base verb After will, would, may, might, can and could, use the base verb without to. It might rain. (not: It might to rain.)

Modals Use Example will / would strong prediction (would is more polite or hypothetical) The new tool will save us time. may / might possible, about 50% We might miss the deadline. can / could possible, a general ability or chance The server could crash under heavy load. May, might and could may, might and could are very close in meaning. might and could sound a little less sure than may.

English Meaning / Spanish hint Example sentence surely seguramente, sin duda The launch will surely attract new users. definitely definitivamente, sin duda We will definitely hit the target this quarter. probably probablemente The client will probably approve the design. might podría (poca seguridad) The meeting might run late. could podría (posibilidad) This change could cause new bugs. forecast pronóstico, prever Our forecast says sales will grow by 10%. on track según lo previsto The project is on track, so we will probably finish early. deadline fecha límite We might miss the deadline if testing takes longer.

Sure Not sure Negative Stand-up update The migration will definitely finish today. The new feature will surely reduce support tickets. Project status email Hi Marta, We are close, but the QA team found two bugs. The release might be delayed by a day or two. We will probably know more after tomorrow's tests. Best, Daniel Planning meeting The vendor will not deliver the hardware before March. I don't think the old system will survive another year. 💬 Sprint planning Ana: Do you think we will finish the login page this sprint? Leo: We will probably finish the design, but the API might not be ready. Ana: Will the client be happy with that? Leo: They will definitely be happy if we show a working demo.

❌ Wrong ✅ Correct Why It might to rain tomorrow. It might rain tomorrow. No to after a modal. She will definitely to join. She will definitely join. Base verb after will. He wills probably finish. He will probably finish. will never takes -s. It will maybe rain. It will probably rain. / It may rain. maybe does not go after will. Use probably, or use may or might. I am thinking it will work. I think it will work. think for an opinion uses the simple form. Spanish speakers In Spanish you can predict with the present (Mañana lo termino) or with the future ending (terminará). In English, use a modal: will, may, might. Also, might is not a past tense here. It talks about the future.

Use will, will not, might or could, and the verb in brackets. I am 100% sure. The update ______ (fix) the bug. I am not sure. The client ______ (ask) for changes. The traffic is terrible. We ______ (arrive) late. I am certain it is impossible. The team ______ (finish) by tomorrow.
Rewrite each sentence with the adverb in brackets. The budget will be approved. (probably) The server will fail during the demo. (definitely not, use won't)
Make three predictions about your next project. Use one sure, one probable and one possible. What will your team probably do next quarter?
You are about 50% sure. Which sentence fits? The release will definitely be late.The release might be late.The release surely is late.

Show answers A. will fix might ask (or could ask) will arrive (or will probably arrive) will not finish (or won't finish) B. The budget will probably be approved. The server definitely won't fail during the demo. C. Answers vary. Check that you use the base verb after the modal and that your certainty words match your meaning.

Show certainty with will surely, will definitely and will not. Show possibility with may, might, could and will probably. Use the base verb after every modal. Put the adverb after will and before won't.

I can order phrases from most sure to least sure. I know when to use will probably and when to use might. I use the base verb without to after modals. I place definitely and probably correctly. I can make three predictions about my work aloud.
Use must to express obligation and to give a confident guess about something you cannot see directly.
Must is a modal verb. It has two main uses. Follow the general modal rules: no -s, and always a base verb after it.
Use must for a strong rule or duty. You must show an ID. He must be paid when the job is done. Structure subject + must + base verb

Use must when you are almost sure something is true, because you have evidence. Wendy's absent; she must be sick. The restaurant is always full; it must have good food. Time Structure Example Present must + base verb She must be tired. Past must have + past participle She must have worked late. Obligation or guess? Look at the context. A rule or order means obligation. A situation with evidence means guess. You must wear a badge. (rule) You must be tired. (guess, you look tired) must not and don't have to are different You mustn't share the password. = it is forbidden. You don't have to attend. = it is not necessary, but you can. Past obligation Must has no past form for obligation. Use had to: We had to submit the report yesterday. Spanish speakers Spanish deber can mean both obligation and guess (debe de estar enfermo). In English, do not use must for a guess about the future. For the future, use will or may. For a guess about the present or past, use must be or must have.

English Meaning / Spanish hint Example sentence obligation obligación Safety training is an obligation for all staff. show an ID mostrar una identificación You must show an ID at the entrance. be paid ser pagado He must be paid when the job is done. absent ausente Wendy is absent today. must be debe de ser / estar (suposición) She must be in a meeting. must have + past participle debe de haber... He must have forgotten the call. mustn't prohibido, no debe You mustn't share client data. have to tener que (obligación externa) We have to submit the form by Friday.

Obligation Confident guess Company policy email All employees must complete the security training by Friday. Visitors must sign in at reception. You mustn't share your password with anyone. Team chat Mia isn't online. She must be in a meeting. The site is down. Someone must have changed the settings. Pedro looks happy. The client must have approved the proposal. 💬 Office conversation Laura: Where is Wendy? She is never late. Dan: She is absent today. She must be sick. Laura: Then we must send her tasks to someone else. Dan: Right. The report must be ready before noon.

❌ Wrong ✅ Correct Why He musts show an ID. He must show an ID. Modals never take -s. You must to wear a badge. You must wear a badge. No to after must. She must sick. She must be sick. Assumptions The notes list object pronouns (you, me, him/her, them) and subject pronouns (I, you, they). This page also adds the rest of the subject, object and possessive set so you see the full picture.
Use subject pronouns before a verb and object pronouns after a verb or a preposition, so your English is clear and not repetitive.

A pronoun replaces a noun. The form changes depending on its job in the sentence. Subject pronoun: it does the action. It goes before the verb. Object pronoun: it receives the action. It follows a verb or a preposition. It can be singular or plural. Subject Object Possessive adjective Possessive pronoun I me my mine you you your yours he him his his she her her hers it it its (rare) we us our ours they them their theirs Subject, verb, object She (subject) sent (verb) them (object) the report. They (subject) called (verb) me (object). Send the file to (preposition) him (object). After a preposition, use an object pronoun with me, for us, to them, about her, from him Between you and me (not: between you and I). It and you it and you have the same form as subject and object. Only the position changes: You called me / I called you. Possessives have no apostrophe It is its, not it's (it is). Write yours, hers, theirs, not your's, her's or their's.

Say where something is in an office, on a screen or in a document, using the main prepositions of position.

A preposition of position shows the place of one thing in relation to another. Structure subject + be + preposition + noun The printer is next to the kitchen. Preposition Meaning Example inside within a space The keys are inside the drawer. outside not within a space The team is waiting outside the meeting room. above / over higher than something The clock is above the door. below lower than something Please sign below the line. on top of touching the upper surface The report is on top of the desk. under / underneath lower, often covered The cables are under the desk. next to / beside at the side, very close My desk is next to the window. between in the middle of two things The meeting room is between the kitchen and my office. in the middle of in the center of something The table is in the middle of the room. in front of at the front, facing The reception is in front of the elevator. at the back of / behind at the rear The storage room is at the back of the office. Above vs over above and over are often the same. Use over when something covers or crosses another thing (a lamp over the table). Use above for a simple higher level (the logo is above the title). Under vs underneath underneath is a little more emphatic than under. It often means something is hidden or covered. Between is for two, among is for many Use between for two things or people: between the printer and the door. For a group of three or more, use among: among the files.

Decide when to use the present perfect (have / has + past participle) and when to use the simple past to talk about the past at work.

Both tenses talk about the past. The difference is the connection to now. Structure Present perfect: have / has + past participle (I have finished.) Simple past: verb + -ed / irregular form (I finished.)

Use the present perfect when: The subject has a past experience: I have managed a remote team. An action started at an unspecified or unknown time and is not finished, or time is not important: She has worked here for three years. An action is finished but still affects the present: The server has crashed, so nobody can log in. In the negative, you talk about something you expected but did not happen: The client hasn't replied yet.

Use the simple past when: The subject did an action in the past: I sent the report. The action began and ended in the past: We worked late last night. The action is not connected to the present: The team launched the product in 2022. In the negative, it says an action did not happen: He didn't attend the meeting. Present perfect Simple past Time Not specific, or still open Finished time (yesterday, last week, in 2022) Link to now Yes No Example I have updated the ticket. I updated the ticket yesterday. Time words Present perfect: ever, never, already, yet, just, for, since, so far, this week Simple past: yesterday, last week, ago, in 2022, when, at 3 pm Do not mix a finished time with the present perfect You cannot say a finished time with have. Say I sent the email yesterday, not I have sent the email yesterday.

Have you ever led a client workshop? already ya (en positivo) I have already sent the invoice. yet todavía, aún (negativo y preguntas) We haven't received the contract yet. just acabar de The build has just finished. for + period durante I have used this tool for two years. since + point in time desde She has worked here since January. so far hasta ahora So far, we have fixed ten bugs. ago hace (tiempo) We launched the app two years ago.

They have not replied since then.

❌ Wrong ✅ Correct Why I have sent the report yesterday. I sent the report yesterday. Finished time word needs the simple past. I worked here for five years. (still works) I have worked here for five years. The action continues now. Did you ever lead a team? Have you ever led a team? ever asks about life experience. She has went to the meeting. She has gone to the meeting. Use the past participle after have / has. When have you joined the company? When did you join the company? When asks for a finished time. Spanish speakers Spanish often uses the simple form for both (Trabajé aquí cinco años and He trabajado aquí cinco años). In English the choice changes the meaning. Ask yourself: is it connected to now? If yes, present perfect. If it is finished, simple past.

Present perfect = past with a link to now (experience, unfinished or recent results). Simple past = finished action, usually with a time. Time words help: for, since, yet, already, ever vs yesterday, ago, last week. Negative: haven't done yet = expected, not yet. didn't do = it did not happen.

Describe routines, rules and automatic results using If + present simple, present simple.

The zero conditional talks about things that always happen. The result is certain. It is the same every time. Structure If + present simple , present simple (condition) (result) Part Verb form Example Condition (if clause) present simple If the team finishes a project, Result (main clause) present simple the manager schedules a review meeting. Two ways to build it You can start with the result. Then you do not need a comma. If a new employee joins, an HR team member explains company policies. An HR team member explains company policies if a new employee joins. If can mean when In the zero conditional, if and when mean almost the same thing: every time this happens. Both are correct. Do not use will in either clause Use the present simple in both parts. will is for the first conditional, which talks about one possible future situation.

Zero conditional First conditional Meaning Always true, routine One possible future event Structure If + present, present If + present, will + base verb Example If the build fails, the pipeline sends an alert. If the build fails today, I will fix it tonight.

Meetings Onboarding Engineering Team rules If the team finishes a project, the manager schedules a review meeting. If someone is absent, they read the meeting notes later. HR process If a new employee joins, an HR team member explains company policies. If a new developer joins, the team lead gives them access to the repositories. Code review & CI If a pull request has no approval, the bot blocks the merge. If the tests fail, the pipeline sends a message to the team channel. 💬 Stand-up chat Ana: What happens if a pull request stays open for two days? Leo: If a pull request stays open for two days, the bot reminds the reviewers. Ana: Great. And if nobody answers? Leo: If nobody answers, the tech lead picks a reviewer.

If the team finishes a project**,** the manager schedules a review. Use a comma when if comes first. If the build fails, it is sending an alert. If the build fails, it sends an alert. Show complete agreement, polite disagreement and partial agreement in a meeting, and use modals to suggest ideas and talk about possible results.

In a meeting, you often need to say if you accept or reject an idea. Choose your phrase by how strong your opinion is and how polite you want to be. Level Phrases Complete agreement I fully agree with/that… · I'm in complete agreement with/that… Complete disagreement I absolutely disagree with/that… · I'm in total disagreement with/that… Polite disagreement I'm afraid I can't agree with/that… · I'm sorry, I disagree with/that… · I have to say, I disagree with/that… Partial agreement I would agree with you, but… · You may be right, but… With or that? After agree with, use a noun or pronoun: I fully agree with Sara. After agree that, use a full clause: I fully agree that we need more testing. Adverbs and adjectives add strength fully, absolutely, complete and total make your opinion strong. Use them when you are sure. Do not use them to disagree with your manager in front of the whole team without a polite opening.

Modal Use Example can possibility We can return the extra money after the project is completed. should advice, a good idea We should try to negotiate for a higher price. might a possible result If we set the price too high, our prospects might back out. could a possible problem Her tardiness could become an issue. Partial agreement is not a yes I would agree with you, but… and You may be right, but… mean you are not sure. The important part comes after but.

Bring up work issues in a clear and polite way by expressing observations, sharing new information and giving reminders, using the present perfect when needed.

When you bring up a work issue, you usually do one of three things. Purpose Example Express an observation I've noticed that our printer hasn't been working properly. Share new information I wanted to let you know the company has a new overtime policy. · I think you should know that our latest product isn't doing so well. Give a reminder I'd like to remind you that using Facebook at work is a major offense.

The present perfect connects a past event with the present. It is useful when the problem started before now and still matters. Structure have/has + past participle It has come to my attention that ... I have noticed that ... Soft openings I've noticed that…, I wanted to let you know… and I think you should know that… prepare the other person. They sound better than starting directly with the problem. Contractions In speaking, use contractions: I've noticed, hasn't been working. In a formal email, It has come to my attention that… is also common. Say the facts, not the blame Describe what you see: The report has not arrived. Avoid You never send the report. Facts are easier to accept.

Use expressions to communicate mindfully with co-workers: check how they feel, offer help, ask for and share opinions, respond kindly, and show appreciation.

Communicating mindfully means you listen, choose your words with care and think about how the other person feels. There are six useful functions. Function Example expressions Checking how someone feels How are you today? · How is your day going so far? Offering help How can I support you? · I would be happy to … Asking for opinions I would appreciate your input on … · What are your thoughts on …? Lead a project review meeting in five steps: set the tone, review the project, review the outcome, ask for feedback, and wrap up.

A project review meeting looks back at a finished project. The goal is to learn what worked, what did not, and what to improve next time. Step Goal Example phrases 1. Setting the tone Thank people, explain the purpose Thank you for attending this project review. · The purpose of this meeting is … 2. Reviewing the project Talk about methods and roles What did we do well? · Which parts were difficult? 3. Reviewing the outcome Check results What did the team accomplish? · Did they make an impact? 4. Asking for feedback and recommendations Collect ideas What can we do better next time? 5. Wrapping up Summarize and thank To recap, … · Thank you for your honest feedback. Start positive Begin with thanks: I appreciate all your efforts in making this project successful. People share more honest feedback when they feel valued. Use the past simple for finished work Most review questions use the past simple because the project is finished: What did we do well?, What did the team accomplish? Talk about the work, not the person Say Which parts of our methods were difficult? instead of Who made mistakes?. A review is not a trial.

An assertive opinion is clear and confident, but still respectful. Three tools help you.

After verbs like support and expressions like put our vote behind, use the -ing form. I/We support having a paperless office. I/We are putting our vote behind exploring business opportunities in China.

Make suggestions with modals and question words, and discuss business options using conditionals and phrases like What if… and An alternative….

I/We suggest ... Let's ... Modals and question words are also useful: Structure Example You/We/He/She/It/They could ... We could move the meeting to Monday. You/We/He/She/They might (not) want to ... You might want to check the numbers again. What/How about ... ? How about using a shared document? Why don't/doesn't you/we/they/he/she/it ... ? Why don't we ask the client? Why not ... ? Why not test it first? Softer or stronger? Let's… and I suggest… are direct. You might want to… and We could… are softer. Use soft forms with your manager or a client. Verb forms after each phrase I suggest + -ing or that clause: I suggest meeting early. Let's + base verb: Let's start now. could, might want to + base verb. What/How about + -ing: How about using a template? Why don't we + base verb: Why don't we ask?

Use the first conditional to compare options and results. If we implement a workforce reduction plan, our company will be able to cope with the global recession. If we freeze hiring employees, we won't have to fire some of our best employees. If we do this, then the company will lose a great deal of talent. Other helpful phrases: Phrase Example What if ... What if we consider outsourcing overseas? An alternative ... An alternative could be stopping all salary increases and bonuses. How about ... How about we implement cost-cutting strategies? Ask for and express opinions in a meeting using verb structures (think, feel, believe) and noun structures (opinion, thoughts, views).

There are two main ways to ask for an opinion and to give one: with verbs or with nouns. Asking for an opinion Giving an opinion Verbs What do you think of/about ... ? I think/feel/believe (that) ... What can you say about ... ? How do you feel about ... ? Nouns What's your opinion of/about/on ... ? In my opinion, ... What are your thoughts/views/comments on/about ... ? I'd like to know your opinion/thoughts on/about ... I'd like to hear your comments on/about ... Pick the right preposition Many of these phrases accept two prepositions: think of/about, opinion of/about/on, thoughts on/about. Both are correct. Choose one and stay consistent. Direct or indirect? Direct question: What do you think of the new design? Indirect, more formal: I'd like to know your opinion on the new design. Use the indirect form with senior people or in formal meetings. Verb or noun after the preposition After of, about and on, use a noun or an -ing form: What do you think about changing the schedule? Do not use the base verb.

(más formal) What are your views on remote work? I'd like to hear your comments on ... me gustaría escuchar tus comentarios sobre ... I'd like to hear your comments on the proposal. Review, adjust and question technical specifications using four key phrases.

Technical specifications (or specs) describe how a product or system must be built. In meetings, you often review, adjust, suggest changes and check if something is possible. Explain scope creep and use infinitives of purpose to set goals, give reasons and communicate limits.

Scope creep happens when the requirements of a project in progress grow, but the schedule, budget and other resources do not change. If nobody manages it, the project often fails. You can avoid it with clear goals and clear limits. To set goals and limits, use infinitives of purpose. They give the reason for an action. Structure action + to + base verb action + so as to + base verb action + in order to + base verb Form Example to + verb Many young entrepreneurs join the tech tour to meet new investors. so as to + verb (formal) The warehouse officer visited different sites so as to ensure stocks are complete. in order to + verb (formal) We wrote a change request in order to protect the budget. negative We froze the scope so as not to delay the launch. Four rules The infinitive can come before or after the main verb. It works with main verbs in different tenses. In formal English, so as to and in order to mean the same as to. For the negative, put not before to: in order not to, so as not to. Before or after the main verb To cut costs for the company, all contract analysts will review documents. All contract analysts will review documents to cut costs for the company. Not for + verb Do not say for to or for plus a verb to give a purpose. Say to cut costs, not for cut costs or for to cut costs. Do not put not after to Say in order not to delay or so as not to delay. Avoid in order to not delay in formal project documents. Plain to has no formal negative, so switch to so as not to or in order not to.

Present a project proposal in a clear order: opening, outline, goals, problem, solution, phases, costs and conclusion.

A good proposal presentation follows a fixed structure. Your audience always knows where you are. Proposal structure 1. Begin the presentation 2. Give an outline 3. State the main idea and goals 4. State the present situation and problems 5. Introduce the solution and actions 6. Move from one part to another 7. Explain stages, phases and deadlines 8. Show the estimated costs (visual aids) 9. Conclude Step Useful sentence Begin Today, I will present our project proposal for Company A's Static Printer. Outline First, I will explain the concept. Then, I will talk about the timeline. After that, I will show you our costings. Goals The project aims to lower energy usage by using static electricity. Problem At the moment, regular inkjet printers use electrical pulses to transfer ink. Solution Because of this, we started brainstorming to create an initial design. Move on For the next part of my presentation, please refer to the table on the screen. Phases Phase 1 will involve building our initial design. Costs As you can see from this chart, the estimated cost is 2 million euros. Conclude In summary, I would like to emphasize how helpful our project can be. Use infinitives to sound professional Infinitives are short and clear when you open, state the aim or change topic. To start this presentation ... The aim of this project is to reduce the operation costs ... I would like to move on to my next topic ... Phases use will Phases and deadlines are plans for the future. Use will involve, will include and will be about. Say one idea per sentence In a live presentation, long sentences are hard to follow. Pause after each step of your outline.

Structures The product has (feature/s) which (function/s). The product, with its (feature/s), (function/s). It can (function). The camera has an improved lens which captures sharper pictures. The app, with its simple menu, saves users a lot of time. It can translate messages in real time.

This desk is made of wood. made from the material changes into something new. Paper is made from wood. Quick test Can you still recognize the material? Use of. Is it now a different thing? Use from.

Causative verbs show what a product allows or causes you to do: let, make, have, get and help. Verb Pattern Example let let + person + base verb It has an improved lens which lets you take sharper pictures. make make + thing + base verb Its compact design makes it fit into a small bag. help help + person + (to) + verb It helps you clean your house without harsh smells. have have + person + base verb The app has users confirm their email first. get get + person + to + verb The reminders get you to finish tasks on time. get needs to After let, make and have, use the base verb. After get, use to + verb. After help, to is optional.

A compound adjective joins two words with a hyphen. It comes before a noun. point-and-shoot cameras germ-killing ingredients mild-smelling bleach Singular only The first part never takes a plural -s. We say a ten-minute demo, not a ten-minutes demo.

English Meaning / Spanish hint Example sentence feature característica The main feature is the fast search. function función One function of this tool is to back up your files. lens lente The phone has an improved lens. compact design diseño compacto Its compact design fits in a pocket. harsh fuerte, agresivo The cleaner has no harsh smells. ingredient ingrediente, componente It has germ-killing ingredients. made of hecho de (el material no cambia) The case is made of aluminum. made from hecho a partir de (el material cambia) The cover is made from recycled plastic. worry about preocuparse por You do not have to worry about passwords.

Product pitch Email Short product pitch Our new speaker has a compact design which lets you carry it anywhere. It is made of aluminum, so it is light and strong. The case is made from recycled plastic. It helps you stay focused with its noise-cancelling microphone. Email to a client Subject: Our new cleaning gel Hello Marta, Our new gel has germ-killing ingredients which keep surfaces safe. Its mild-smelling formula makes it easy to use in small offices. Best regards, Daniel 💬 Product demo call Client: What makes this camera different? Sales rep: It has an improved lens which lets you take sharper pictures, even at night. Client: Is it easy to carry? Sales rep: Yes. Its compact design makes it fit into a pocket. It is a point-and-shoot camera, so it is simple to use.

❌ Wrong ✅ Correct Why Paper is made of wood. Paper is made from wood. The wood changes into paper. The app lets you to share files. The app lets you share files. No to after let. It makes you to save time. It makes you save time. No to after make. a ten-minutes video a ten-minute video A compound adjective stays singular. It helps you cleaning. It helps you clean (or to clean). help + base verb or to + verb. Spanish speakers In Spanish we say hace que puedas hacer, te permite hacer. In English, do not add to or that after let and make: It lets you work offline.

This table is ______ (made of / made from) steel. Cheese is ______ (made of / made from) milk. The app lets you ______ (create) reports quickly. Its bright screen makes it ______ (be) easy to read outside.
Rewrite each sentence with a compound adjective or a causative verb. The soap has ingredients that kill germs. The new design allows the phone to fit in a small pocket. (use makes)
Describe a product you use every day. Use has ... which ... and one causative verb. What is your phone made of? Use made of and made from correctly.
Choose the correct sentence. It lets you to take sharper pictures.It lets you take sharper pictures.It lets you taking sharper pictures.

Show answers A. made of made from create be B. The soap has germ-killing ingredients. The new design makes the phone fit into a small pocket. C. Answers vary. Check that you use the base verb after let and make, and of or from correctly.

Use The product has ... which ... and It can ... to describe features. made of = the material stays the same. made from = the material changes. let, make, have + base verb. get + to + verb. help + (to) + verb. Compound adjectives use hyphens and stay singular: germ-killing, mild-smelling.

I can describe a product with has ... which .... I know when to use made of and made from. I can use lets you and makes it correctly. I can create two compound adjectives. I can present a product aloud in three sentences.

documents.s: How to discuss using AI tools at work

documents.t: Ask colleagues about the AI tools they use, ask follow-up questions, and describe what AI tools do in simple language.
Questions Do you use any AI tools in your team? How does that help? Do you use any other tools? Start with a general question. Then ask a follow-up question to get details.

Structure Use Example I use AI to + verb a specific task I use AI to summarize long documents. I use AI for + noun / -ing a general purpose I use AI for brainstorming ideas. AI helps me (to) + verb a benefit AI helps me organize information faster. I mainly use it when... when you usually use it I mainly use it when I write emails.
To describe a product in a simple way, use a present simple verb after It: Structure It checks / saves / gives / ... + object It checks my grammar. It saves me time. It gives me ideas for titles.

Useful phrases It makes it easier to ... It allows us to ... It can help us ... It saves us time by + -ing It makes it easier to understand complex topics. It saves us time by automating repetitive tasks. Always -ing after a preposition After by, for and other prepositions, use the -ing form: by automating, for brainstorming. to or by? Use to after verbs like help, want and need. Use by to explain a method or action: It helps us by explaining new ideas.
documents.s: Talk about results: It + verb + to / by + -ing

documents.t: English Meaning / Spanish hint Example sentence AI tool herramienta de IA Do you use any AI tools in your team? summarize resumir I use AI to summarize long documents. brainstorm hacer una lluvia de ideas I use AI for brainstorming ideas. repetitive task tarea repetitiva It automates repetitive tasks. organize information organizar información AI helps me organize information more quickly. mainly principalmente I mainly use it for emails. save time ahorrar tiempo It saves us time by writing first drafts. make it easier to facilitar It makes it easier to find old files.

💬 Chat in the break room Sam: Do you use any AI tools in your team? Rosa: Yes. I use AI to summarize meeting notes. Sam: How does that help? Rosa: It saves me time by writing a short summary for me. Sam: Do you use any other tools? Rosa: I also use one for brainstorming ideas. It gives me many options. Stand-up Email Stand-up update I mainly use AI when I write test cases. It checks my code and gives me ideas. AI helps me find bugs more quickly. Email to the team Subject: AI tools in our team Hi everyone, I use AI for writing first drafts of reports. It saves us time by automating repetitive tasks. Do you use any other tools that help the team? Thanks, Julia

❌ Wrong ✅ Correct Why It saves us time by automate tasks. It saves us time by automating tasks. Use -ing after by. It helps us to by learning AI. It helps us by learning about AI. Do not put to and by together. I use AI for summarize documents. I use AI to summarize documents (or for summarizing). to + verb or for + -ing. AI helps me to organizing ideas. AI helps me organize (or to organize) ideas. Base verb or to + verb. It makes easier to write. It makes it easier to write. You need it after makes. Spanish speakers Spanish uses the infinitive after a preposition (por automatizar). English uses -ing: by automating. Also, do not say I use AI for to ....
I use AI ______ (summarize) long documents. It saves us time by ______ (automate) repetitive tasks. I use AI for ______ (brainstorm) ideas. It makes ______ easier to understand complex topics.
I use AI for summarize reports. (correct it) AI organizes information. This helps me. (combine with helps me)
Ask a colleague about their AI tools. Use one general question and two follow-ups. Explain how you use AI at work. Use I use AI to ... and It saves me time by ....
Choose the correct sentence. It saves us time by automate tasks.It saves us time by automating tasks.It saves us time by to automate tasks.

Show answers A. to summarize automating brainstorming it B. I use AI to summarize reports. (or I use AI for summarizing reports.) AI helps me organize information. C. Answers vary. Check that you ask follow-ups such as How does that help? and use -ing after by.

Ask: Do you use any AI tools in your team? then How does that help? Habits: I use AI to + verb, I use AI for + noun / -ing, AI helps me (to) + verb. Describe tools: It checks / saves / gives .... Results: It makes it easier to ..., It saves us time by + -ing.

I can ask a general question and a follow-up question. I can use I use AI to and I use AI for correctly. I always use -ing after by. I can describe a tool with It checks / saves / gives. I can explain how AI helps me at work.

documents.s: How AI is shaping today's customer support

documents.t: Learn and use five key words to talk about AI in customer support: agents, virtual assistants, transforming, personal touch and alongside.

AI is changing how companies help their customers. Today, people and AI tools often work together. These five words help you talk about this change. Word Meaning Example from the lesson agents employees who help customers with questions and problems Travel agents give tourists helpful information about hotels and flights. virtual assistants AI-powered tools that help users by answering questions and completing tasks The virtual assistants in M&P's mobile phone models can translate messages and suggest replies. transforming changing something completely to make it better The fresh paint is transforming the plain house into a bright place. personal touch special care or attention that makes someone feel important Isa wrote a note to add a personal touch to the gift. alongside together with something or someone A nurse and a doctor work alongside each other to care for patients in the clinic. Word partners transform ... into ...: AI is transforming support into a faster service. add a personal touch: Agents add a personal touch to every reply. work alongside: Agents work alongside virtual assistants. Agent in different contexts In customer support, an agent is a person on the support team. A travel agent or a real estate agent also helps customers, but in other industries. transforming is the -ing form Use is / are transforming for a change that is happening now. For a finished change, use transformed: AI has transformed support. alongside is one word Write alongside, not along side. It is followed by a noun: alongside agents, alongside our team.

English Meaning / Spanish hint Example sentence agent agente, representante de atención A support agent answered my question in two minutes. virtual assistant asistente virtual The virtual assistant suggested three answers. transform transformar AI is transforming the way we answer tickets. personal touch toque personal A friendly name adds a personal touch. alongside junto a, al lado de Chatbots work alongside human agents. answer questions responder preguntas Virtual assistants answer common questions 24 hours a day. complete tasks completar tareas The tool can complete simple tasks, like resetting a password. suggest replies sugerir respuestas It suggests replies, and the agent chooses one.

Team meeting Email to a client Support team meeting AI is transforming our support team. Virtual assistants answer simple questions, so agents have more time for difficult cases. Agents work alongside the assistants and add a personal touch to each reply. Email to a client Subject: Our new support service Dear Mr. Lopez, Our virtual assistant is available 24 hours a day to answer common questions. Our agents work alongside it and add a personal touch when you need extra help. Kind regards, Elena 💬 Talking about a new tool Manager: How is the new virtual assistant changing our work? Agent: It is transforming our daily routine. It handles easy questions and suggests replies. Manager: Do customers still need agents? Agent: Yes. We work alongside the assistant, and we add a personal touch to difficult cases.

❌ Wrong ✅ Correct Why Agents work along side the assistant. Agents work alongside the assistant. alongside is one word. AI transform our support. AI is transforming our support. Use the right verb form for a change in progress. We add a personal touch for each reply. We add a personal touch to each reply. add ... to .... The virtual assistant are fast. The virtual assistant is fast. Singular subject, singular verb. Virtual assistant can answer questions. A virtual assistant can answer questions. (or Virtual assistants can ...) Use an article or a plural. Spanish speakers Do not translate agent as agente in every case. In customer support it means the person who helps the customer. Also, watch the false friend assist: it means ayudar, not asistir a una reunión (that is attend).

Use: agents, virtual assistants, transforming, personal touch, alongside. Human ______ answer the difficult questions. The ______ can translate messages and suggest replies. AI is ______ the way companies help their customers. A short handwritten note adds a ______ to the gift. Our team works ______ the chatbot.
AI changes our support completely. (use is transforming) The agents and the tool work together. (use alongside)
How does your company use AI in customer support? Use at least three of the new words. Give an example of a personal touch in customer service.
What does 'personal touch' mean? A tool that answers questions automaticallySpecial care that makes someone feel importantA phone with a touch screen

Show answers A. agents virtual assistants transforming personal touch alongside B. AI is transforming our support. The agents work alongside the tool. C. Answers vary. Check that you use the words in correct sentences.

agents = employees who help customers. virtual assistants = AI tools that answer questions and complete tasks. transforming = changing something completely to make it better. personal touch = special care that makes someone feel important. alongside = together with.

I can define the five words in my own words. I can make a sentence with each word. I know the word partners: add a personal touch to, work alongside. I can explain how AI and agents work together. I can describe a support change using is transforming.
Respond to negative feedback from a client in a calm, professional way. Apologize, show empathy, explain the solution and keep a friendly tone.

A good response has several steps. You do not need all of them every time, but the order helps. Apologize. Clarify the problem. Show empathy. Take responsibility. Explain how and when you will solve it. Offer an alternative. Summarize. Promise a follow-up. End with a friendly tone.

Step Useful phrases Apologize First of all, I'd like to say how sorry I am. / I'm so (very, really, terribly) sorry about that. / I apologize for ... / Let me apologize for ... Clarify If I understand you correctly, ... / Could you please tell me exactly what happened? / Could you explain ... a little more? / Would you mind if I just check ... again? Show empathy I can see why ... / I understand. / I see what you mean. / I would feel the same way. / What a difficult situation this puts you in. Take responsibility It looks like an oversight on our part. / There seems to be a misunderstanding. / It appears ... got overlooked. / I'm afraid there has been some sort of mix-up. Explain the solution I'll take care of this at once for you. / I'm sure we can find a solution. / This should be resolved by the end of ... / You'll receive ... by ... Offer an alternative May I offer ... as an alternative for ...? / I'll look into other possible ways of ... / Perhaps you could consider ... as another option. Summarize What we have decided is ... / Our action plan is ... / I'd like to review this once more to make sure we agree. Follow up I'll get back to you ... / I'll make sure that ... End friendly Thanks for bringing this to our attention. / Is there anything else I can help you with today? Clarify before you promise Repeat the problem in your own words: If I understand you correctly, the invoice shows the wrong amount. This shows you are listening. Softening responsibility Phrases like There seems to be a misunderstanding and It looks like an oversight are soft and polite. Use them to accept the issue without blaming a person. Apologize with for Use apologize for + noun or -ing: I apologize for the delay. / I apologize for sending the wrong file.

English Meaning / Spanish hint Example sentence apologize disculparse Let me apologize for the delay. oversight descuido, omisión It looks like an oversight on our part. mix-up confusión, equivocación There has been some sort of mix-up with your order. get overlooked pasarse por alto It appears your request got overlooked. at once de inmediato I'll take care of this at once. make up for compensar We'd like to offer a discount to make up for this inconvenience. resolve resolver This should be resolved by Friday. alternative alternativa May I offer a refund as an alternative? get back to you volver a contactarte I'll get back to you tomorrow morning.

💬 Phone call with an unhappy client Client: I paid for the premium plan, but my account still shows the free plan. Agent: First of all, I'm terribly sorry about that. If I understand you correctly, your payment worked but the plan did not change? Client: Exactly. This is the second time. Agent: I can see why you are upset. It looks like an oversight on our part. I'll take care of this at once for you. Client: How long will it take? Agent: This should be resolved by the end of today. I'll get back to you this afternoon. Email reply Call summary Reply to a client complaint Subject: RE: Wrong invoice Dear Ms. Rivera, Thank you for bringing this to our attention. Let me apologize for the mix-up with your invoice. It looks like an oversight on our part. You'll receive a corrected invoice by tomorrow at noon. I'd be glad to offer a 10 percent discount to make up for this inconvenience. Please reach out again should you have any more concerns. Kind regards, Andrés End of a call What we have decided is this: we will send a corrected file today. Our action plan is to review your account and confirm the change by Friday. I'd like to review this once more to make sure we agree. I'll make sure that you receive a confirmation email. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

❌ Wrong ✅ Correct Why I apologize by the delay. I apologize for the delay. apologize for. Can you explain me what happened? Could you tell me exactly what happened? / Could you explain to me... explain needs to before a person. It was your fault. There seems to be a misunderstanding. Avoid blame. Use a polite, neutral phrase. I will resolve at once your problem. I'll take care of this at once for you. / I'll resolve your problem at once. Do not put at once between the verb and its object. I'll make sure that you will receive it. I'll make sure that you receive it. Use the present simple after make sure that for a future result. Spanish speakers Do not write I am sorry for the inconveniences just because inconvenientes is plural in Spanish. Use the singular: the inconvenience. Also avoid It is your fault (es su culpa). It sounds rude in English.
First of all, I'm terribly ______ about that. If I ______ you correctly, the file did not arrive. It looks like an ______ on our part. I'll get ______ to you by Friday.
Make each sentence more polite and professional. It is your mistake. Tell me what happened.
Role-play an unhappy client call. Use at least one phrase from each of these steps: apologize, empathy, solution and follow-up. A client says, "Your app lost my data!" What do you say first?
Which phrase shows empathy? It is not our problem.I can see why you are upset.You should read the instructions.

Show answers A. sorry understand oversight back B. There seems to be a misunderstanding. (or It looks like an oversight on our part.) Could you please tell me exactly what happened? C. Answers vary. Check that you apologize first, repeat the problem, show empathy, say when you will fix it, and promise a follow-up.

Start with an apology: I apologize for ..., I'm terribly sorry about that. Clarify and show empathy: If I understand you correctly, ..., I can see why .... Take responsibility softly: It looks like an oversight on our part. Say how and when: This should be resolved by ..., I'll get back to you .... End friendly: Is there anything else I can help you with today?

I can apologize with three different phrases. I can repeat the client's problem with If I understand you correctly. I can show empathy without blaming anyone. I can explain how and when I will fix a problem. I can offer an alternative and promise a follow-up. I can end the conversation in a friendly way.
Describe what a desktop, mobile or web app does, compare its pros and cons, and explain its plans and prices.
You can talk about an app in three steps: functions, pros and cons, and pricing.

Useful structures This ... app offers ... ... (also) helps / enables / allows ... to ... ... uses / makes use of ... to ... ... is (also) ..., especially for ... ... has ... features ... This project management app offers a clear task board. It also helps teams to track their work. The app makes use of AI to sort your emails. It is great, especially for remote teams. Verb patterns allow and enable need a person + to: It allows users to share files. help can use to or not: It helps you save time.

Useful structures On the plus side, ... One of the downsides (of) ... The disadvantage(s) (of ...) is / are balanced by ... On the plus side, the app works offline. One of the downsides of the free version is the limited storage. The disadvantage of the price is balanced by the great support.

Useful structures ... starts / starting at ... ... costs ... per / a month / year, billed yearly / annually. ... will cost you ... per / a month / year per user. The Basic plan starts at 8 dollars a month, billed annually. The Team plan will cost you 12 dollars a month per user. Billed yearly billed annually and billed yearly mean you pay once a year, not every month. per and a Say per month or a month. Both are correct. Do not say for month.

English Meaning / Spanish hint Example sentence offer ofrecer This app offers a simple dashboard. enable permitir, habilitar It enables teams to work together in real time. make use of hacer uso de, aprovechar The app makes use of your calendar. on the plus side como punto a favor On the plus side, it is free to start. downside desventaja One downside is the lack of offline mode. be balanced by compensarse con The cost is balanced by the time you save. plan plan, suscripción The Pro plan includes extra storage. per user por usuario It costs 10 dollars per user. billed annually facturado anualmente The plan starts at 99 dollars, billed annually.

Team chat Email to manager Message to the team I tried the new note-taking app. It allows us to share notes in real time. On the plus side, it is easy to use. One of the downsides is that there is no offline mode. It starts at 6 dollars a month per user, billed annually. Email to manager Subject: Proposal for a new design tool Hi Carla, This web app helps designers to work on the same file. It is especially good for remote teams. The Team plan will cost us 15 dollars a month per user, billed yearly. The price is balanced by the time we save in reviews. Best, Ben 💬 Choosing an app in a meeting Nora: What does this mobile app offer? Tom: It enables us to scan documents and send them to the cloud. It is especially useful for field staff. Nora: Any downsides? Tom: One of the downsides is the battery use. But that is balanced by the speed. Nora: And the price? Tom: It starts at 5 dollars a month, billed annually.

❌ Wrong ✅ Correct Why It allows to share files. It allows users to share files. allow needs a person before to. It costs 10 dollars for month. It costs 10 dollars per month. Use per or a. On the plus side is the price low. On the plus side, the price is low. Normal word order after the phrase. The disadvantage are balanced by the speed. The disadvantage is balanced by the speed. The verb agrees with disadvantage. It starts in 8 dollars. It starts at 8 dollars. Use at with prices. Spanish speakers Spanish says Permite compartir archivos. English needs the person: It allows you to share files. Also, billed annually is not facturado anual, so do not drop the -ed.

This app ______ us to share files with clients. ______ the plus side, the app is free to start. One of the ______ of this tool is the high price. The Pro plan ______ at 20 dollars a month, billed annually.
Rewrite each sentence with the phrase in brackets. The app is good for freelancers. (especially for) The app uses AI. It sorts your emails. (uses ... to)
Describe an app you use at work. What does it offer? Give one pro and one con. Explain the price of a plan you know. Use starts at and billed annually.
Choose the correct sentence. It will cost you 10 dollars for month per user.It will cost you 10 dollars a month per user.It will cost you 10 dollars at month per user.

Show answers A. allows (or enables) On downsides (or disadvantages) starts B. The app is great, especially for freelancers. The app uses AI to sort your emails. C. Answers vary. Check for one function, one pro, one con, and per month or billed annually.

Functions: This app offers ..., It helps / enables / allows ... to .... Pros and cons: On the plus side, ..., One of the downsides of .... Balance: The disadvantage is balanced by .... Pricing: starts at ..., costs ... per month, billed annually.

I can describe three functions of an app. I can give one pro and one con with the right phrases. I use allow and enable with a person + to. I can say a price with per month and billed annually. I can recommend an app aloud in 30 seconds.
Name the basic rooms of a house and the furniture usually found in each one, so you can describe your home in small talk or for remote work.

Each room has typical furniture. Learn them together: room + furniture. Room Furniture and items Living room coffee table, sofa / couch, chair Dining room dining table, sideboard / buffet Kitchen kitchen table, kitchen cabinets, kitchen island Bathroom sink, tub / shower, flush toilet Bedroom bed, side tables, cabinet / closet Two words, one thing A slash means two words with the same meaning. sofa and couch are the same. sideboard and buffet are the same. cabinet and closet are close in meaning here: a place to keep things. Use there is and there are to describe a room There is a sofa in the living room. (one thing) There are two chairs in the kitchen. (more than one thing) Countable nouns need an article Say a sofa, a sink, a bed. For plural nouns, use a number or no article: two chairs, kitchen cabinets. Spanish speakers Closet in English is usually a place for clothes, like an armario empotrado. A cabinet is a piece of furniture with doors and shelves. Also, sink can be in the kitchen or the bathroom: Spanish uses two words (fregadero, lavabo), English uses one.

English Meaning / Spanish hint Example sentence living room sala de estar, salón We have our video calls in the living room. coffee table mesa de centro My laptop is on the coffee table. sofa / couch sofá There is a comfortable sofa in the living room. dining table mesa del comedor I work at the dining table on busy days. sideboard / buffet aparador The plates are in the sideboard. kitchen island isla de cocina We have breakfast at the kitchen island. kitchen cabinets gabinetes de cocina The kitchen cabinets are white. sink lavabo, fregadero There is a sink in the bathroom and in the kitchen. tub / shower bañera / ducha The bathroom has a tub and a shower. flush toilet inodoro con cisterna The apartment has a flush toilet and a small sink. side table mesita de noche, mesa auxiliar I keep my phone on the side table. closet armario, clóset My jackets are in the closet.

Small talk Email to HR Chat before a meeting Where do you work from home? I work in the living room. There is a coffee table, but I use the dining table as a desk. Home office equipment Hello, I work from home in a small apartment. There is a chair in the dining room, but there is no desk. Could the company help with a table for my workspace? Thank you, Julia 💬 Remote onboarding call Mia: Is that your living room behind you? Daniel: Yes. There is a sofa on the left and a coffee table in front of me. Mia: Nice. Do you have a separate room for work? Daniel: No. I use the dining table. My laptop is next to the sideboard.

❌ Wrong ✅ Correct Why There is two chairs in the kitchen. There are two chairs in the kitchen. Plural noun, so use are. I sleep in the dining room. I sleep in the bedroom. Dining room is for meals. I put my clothes in the kitchen cabinet. I put my clothes in the closet. A closet is for clothes. I have breakfast in the living table. I have breakfast at the dining table. The correct word is dining table. There is sofa in my living room. There is a sofa in my living room. Singular countable nouns need a or the.

Use: sink, bed, sofa, kitchen island, dining table. I sleep in a big ______ in the bedroom. We watch TV on the ______ in the living room. There is a ______ in the bathroom for washing your hands. We eat dinner at the ______ in the dining room. I prepare coffee at the ______ in the kitchen.
Write the sentence with there is or there are. Two chairs are in the living room. Three cabinets are in the kitchen. A tub is in the bathroom.
Describe the living room in your home. What furniture is there? Where do you work from home? What furniture do you use? Describe your bedroom in four sentences.
Which room usually has a kitchen island? The bedroomThe kitchenThe bathroom

Show answers A. bed sofa sink dining table kitchen island B. There are two chairs in the living room. There are three cabinets in the kitchen. There is a tub in the bathroom. C. Answers vary. Check that you use there is and there are correctly and name real furniture.

Learn furniture together with its room. Living room: coffee table, sofa / couch, chair. Kitchen: kitchen table, cabinets, island. Bathroom: sink, tub / shower, toilet. Bedroom: bed, side tables, cabinet / closet. Dining room: dining table, sideboard / buffet. Use there is for one thing and there are for many.

I can name the five basic rooms. I can name two or three pieces of furniture for each room. I know that sofa and couch mean the same thing. I use there is and there are correctly. I can describe my own home in four sentences.

Assumptions This is a vocabulary lesson. The twelve target words come from the class notes. The empathetic-listening phrases in section 3 and 4 are standard English phrases added to help you use the words in real conversations.
Learn twelve useful words and phrases and use them, with simple listening phrases, to show empathy in workplace conversations.

Empathy means understanding how another person feels. An empathetic listener listens to understand, not only to answer. Word or phrase Meaning come naturally happen easily and without effort undisputed accepted or recognized by everyone flawed having a mistake or weakness biases opinions or ideas that can lead to unfair judgment of a group or idea get to the bottom of discover and understand the real reason or truth engage in participate or be part of common ground shared interests or opinions among different parties disclose reveal or make known deepens makes something more serious or more strongly felt reframing changing the way something is done or considered tap into access and use a resource to your advantage audit an official and thorough examination Collocations to remember come naturally to someone: Leading a team comes naturally to her. engage in + noun or -ing: engage in a conversation, engage in learning. find common ground with someone. get to the bottom of + a problem: get to the bottom of the issue. Word forms bias is singular; biases is plural. Everyone has a bias. We must check our biases. disclose is a verb; disclosure is the noun. deepens is the third person of deepen. Add -s when the subject is singular: Listening deepens trust. audit is a noun, and also a verb In the lesson, audit is a noun (a safety audit). You can also use it as a verb: We audit our accounts every year. Spanish speakers Disclose does not mean "disculpar" or "descubrir". It means to reveal information (divulgar). Biases means sesgos or prejuicios. And engage in means to take part in an activity. It does not mean "comprometerse a algo" in every case.

English Meaning / Spanish hint Example sentence come naturally darse con naturalidad, ser fácil para alguien Leadership and team communication come naturally to Ben. undisputed indiscutible The chef is undisputed as the best in the city. flawed defectuoso, con fallas The flawed software crashed and delayed the work. biases sesgos, prejuicios The survey shows biases that affect customers' choices. get to the bottom of llegar al fondo de, descubrir la causa real We need to get to the bottom of this problem. engage in participar en Tom and Phil engage in weekly safety training. common ground puntos en común The two companies found common ground in community service. disclose revelar, divulgar The researchers agreed to disclose their findings. deepens profundiza, intensifica Reading deepens Kurt's understanding of current events. reframing replantear, ver desde otro ángulo Carl approached the project by reframing it as a chance to learn. tap into aprovechar, sacar partido de The factory will tap into modern equipment to produce more. audit auditoría The safety audit showed areas to improve.

English Use Example sentence It sounds like you are feeling... reflect the feeling It sounds like you are feeling frustrated with the deadline. Tell me more about that. invite the person to continue Tell me more about that. What happened next? What I hear you saying is... summarize to check understanding What I hear you saying is that the workload is too high. That must be hard. show understanding That must be hard. How can I help? I may be wrong, but... be aware of your own biases I may be wrong, but I think we can find common ground.

One-to-one Team conflict Email Manager and team member It sounds like you are feeling stressed about the new project. Tell me more about that. I want to get to the bottom of what is making it difficult. Mediating a disagreement Let's engage in a calm conversation and look for common ground. Each of us has biases, so let's listen first. Email after a client call Hi Ana, Thank you for sharing your concerns. What I hear you saying is that the old process was flawed. Watch the spelling back up is a verb (two words): Please back up your files. backup is a noun or adjective (one word): We have a backup. It is a backup file. The same rule works for log in (verb) and login (noun). Phrasal verbs back up, filter out, opt in and opt out are phrasal verbs. Keep the two parts together. Understand the meaning of ten common prefixes and use them to build and guess new words in workplace English.

A prefix goes at the beginning of a base word. It changes the meaning and creates a new word. The base word does not change. Structure prefix + base word = new word un- + happy = unhappy re- + write = rewrite Prefix Meaning Example from the lesson Spanish hint anti- against antibiotics anti-, contra pro- in favor of, supporting pro-war pro-, a favor de pre- before preschool pre-, antes de post- after postgraduate post-, después de ex- former, previous ex-president ex-, antiguo in- not, the opposite of informal in-, no im- not, the opposite of impossible im-, no non- not, without nonsmoking no, sin un- not, the opposite of unhappy no, des- re- again rewrite re-, otra vez Four prefixes, one idea: "not" in-, im-, non- and un- all make the opposite meaning. Learn each one with the words you hear most often. There is no easy rule for which one to use. im- comes before b, m and p im- is a spelling form of in-. We usually use im- before the letters b, m, p: impossible, impolite, immature, imbalance. Hyphens Use a hyphen with ex- (ex-manager) and often with pro- or anti- when the word is new or unusual. Most other prefixes join the word directly: preschool, unhappy, rewrite. When you are not sure, check a dictionary. Spanish speakers Do not translate Spanish prefixes word by word. In English, un- is very common (unclear, unavailable), but Spanish uses des-, in- or no in similar cases. Also, ex- means former, not external: an ex-colleague is a person who used to be your colleague.

How to make it: Push your lips forward a little. Put your tongue near the roof of your mouth without touching it. Push air continuously — like a long, soft 'shhh'. Key difference: This sound does not exist in standard Spanish. The important surprise is that it is written three different ways in English. Spelling pattern 1 — sh: The most common. What you see is what you get. Spelling pattern 2 — ti / ci / si: Hidden. The letters ti, ci, and si before an unstressed vowel make the /ʃ/ sound. This is the most common mistake for Spanish speakers. Spelling pattern 3 — ch (French origin): A false friend. In Spanish, ch = /tʃ/ (like chico). In words borrowed from French, ch = /ʃ/. How to make it: Put your tongue on the roof of your mouth, like you are going to say 'd'. Then let air out softly, like a 'zh' sound. The two sounds happen very fast together. Key difference: The Spanish 'j' is guttural — it comes from the throat (like in jamón). The English /dʒ/ is soft and comes from the tongue touching the roof of the mouth. Like the SH sound, it is written three different ways. Spelling pattern 1 — j: Direct and easy. Spelling pattern 2 — g before e or i: A false friend. In Spanish, g before e/i makes the guttural /x/ sound (like gente). In English, g before e/i always makes /dʒ/ (like gentle). Spelling pattern 3 — dge / ge at the end: The letters dge and ge at the end of a word make /dʒ/. The 'd' and the final 'e' are both silent. A quick reference of board games to play with friends, with a short explanation of how each one works and where to play it online.

Catan is a resource-trading and building game for 3–4 players. The board is made of hexagonal tiles (wood, brick, wool, grain, ore), and each tile has a number token. On your turn you roll two dice: every tile matching the result produces resources for the players with a settlement or city next to it. You spend resources to build roads, settlements, cities, or buy development cards, and you can trade with other players or the bank. Settlements give 1 victory point, cities give 2, and some cards and bonuses (longest road, largest army) give more. The first player to reach 10 victory points wins. Play online: Colonist.io (free, in the browser). Official site: catan.com.

Dudo (also known as Cacho or Liar's Dice) is a bluffing dice game for 2 or more players. Each player has a cup with 5 dice and rolls them in secret. In turn, players make a bid about how many dice of a given face there are in total across all cups (for example, "five 4s"). The next player must either raise the bid (more dice or a higher face) or call "Dudo!" to challenge it. Then all cups are revealed: if the bid was true, the challenger loses a die; if it was false, the bidder loses one. The last player with dice left wins. House rules vary, such as whether 1s are wild. Play online: Play Liar's Dice.

Secret Hitler is a social deduction game for 5–10 players. Each player secretly receives a role: Liberal, Fascist, or Hitler (a Fascist who must stay hidden). Every round, the president nominates a chancellor and everyone votes. If approved, the president draws three policy cards, discards one, and passes two to the chancellor, who enacts one. Liberals win by enacting five Liberal policies or by killing Hitler; Fascists win by enacting six Fascist policies or by electing Hitler as chancellor after three Fascist policies are in place. Talking, bluffing, and accusing are the heart of the game. Play online: Secret Hitler Online. Official site: secrethitler.com.

Codenames is a word-association team game for 4 or more players. Twenty-five word cards are laid out in a 5x5 grid. Two teams (red and blue) each have a spymaster who knows which words belong to their team. The spymaster gives a one-word clue plus a number ("Ocean, 3"), and teammates guess words that match it. A correct guess lets them keep guessing; a wrong one ends the turn and may help the other team. If a team touches the assassin card, it loses immediately. The first team to find all its agents wins. Play online: Codenames Online.
This prompt is designed to generate a full-body cartoon illustration of a real person, based on reference photos you provide. Here's how to use it effectively.
documents.s: How to Use the Cartoon Illustration Prompt

documents.t: 2–5 clear reference photos of the person you want to cartoonize A cartoon style reference image (the prompt calls it cartoon_reference.png) — this is a sample image that shows the art style you want the AI to replicate Access to an AI image generator that accepts image inputs (like GPT-4o, Gemini, or a similar multimodal model)

Gather multiple photos of the person. For best results: Include at least one full-body photo so the AI can read the person's build and proportions Add a front-facing photo for facial features Include photos showing their typical clothing

Find or create a sample cartoon image (cartoon_reference.png) that represents the exact art style you want — clean black outlines, cell-shaded colors, vibrant solid tones (think classic comic book or animated series style).

In the prompt, locate this part: [REFERENCE_PHOTOS] You can either: Leave it as-is if your tool automatically links uploaded images as inputs Replace it with a short note, for example: [REFERENCE_PHOTOS of John Smith, full-body and face shots]
In your AI tool of choice: Upload all your reference photos Upload your cartoon_reference.png style image Paste the full prompt into the message/instructions field Submit
documents.s: Step 4 — Upload Everything and Run the Prompt

documents.t: Check that the result: ✅ Matches the person's body type and proportions ✅ Uses the correct art style (clean lines, cel-shading) ✅ Shows a full-body, forward-facing pose ✅ Has a transparent or grid background ✅ Has no extra text, logos, or other characters

Tip Why It Helps Use well-lit, high-resolution photos The AI reads physical details more accurately Include photos from different angles Helps the AI build a fuller model of the person Use a strong style reference image The more specific the reference, the more consistent the style Be explicit about body type in the placeholder Adds a safety net if photos are ambiguous

You don't need to specify these — they're already baked into the prompt: Full-body, front-facing pose Transparent/grid background No text or logos in the output Clothing folds and stylized textures Faithful replication of the person's build (stocky, thin, athletic, etc.) --

prompt Generate a full-body, standalone cartoon illustration of a single person, based on the specific reference photos provided [REFERENCE_PHOTOS]. The artistic style must be a high-quality, clean-line comic-book illustration, identical to the style seen in cartoon_reference.png, with defined black outlines, cell-shaded coloring, and solid, vibrant tones. The cartoon must faithfully replicate the specific body type, build, and physical proportions of the person in the reference photos, stylized for animation but recognizable. For example, if the person has a stocky build, ensure the cartoon figure is stocky; if they are thin, make the cartoon figure thin, with clothes fitting appropriately. The pose should be a full-body stand, facing forward. The person should have a characteristic expression and wear attire (like their most common or distinctive clothes) seen in the reference photos. The clothing folds and texture should be stylized, following the detailed look of cartoon_reference.png. The background must be completely transparent or a transparency grid pattern, identical to the background of cartoon_reference.png. Do not add any text, logos, or other figures. ### Instrucciones de uso para el usuario: 1. **Sube tus fotos:** Pasa a Nano Banana múltiples fotos de la persona que quieres caricaturizar. Asegúrate de que haya fotos de cuerpo entero para que la IA pueda captar la complexión. 2. **Completa el marcador:** Donde dice `[REFERENCE_PHOTOS]`, puedes escribir una breve nota opcional sobre las fotos, o simplemente dejarlo así si el sistema sabe que son las fotos de entrada. Por ejemplo: `[REFERENCE_PHOTOS de Juan Pérez]`. 3. **Asegúrate de una pose de cuerpo entero:** El prompt especifica una pose de cuerpo entero, así que Nano Banana se centrará en eso. He generado esta imagen para confirmar que entiendo el estilo y la complexión de cuerpo entero requerida: * **Sujeto genérico:** Un hombre con una chaqueta de cuero y vaqueros. * **Estilo:** Idéntico estilo de línea limpia y cel-shaded de cartoon_reference.png. * **Pose:** Cuerpo entero, de pie, mirando hacia adelante. * **Fondo:** Transparente con cuadrícula. Esta imagen demuestra que puedo replicar el estilo y el formato sin usar figuras políticas.
A quick reference of fun online games to play with friends or alone.

Gartic Phone is a multiplayer drawing and guessing game. Each player writes a sentence, then the next player draws it, then another player describes the drawing, and so on. At the end, everyone sees the funny chain of mistakes. It works great in groups and runs directly in the browser — no download needed.

Stopots is a fast-paced word game based on the classic "Stop" or "Categories" game. Players choose a random letter and must fill in categories like countries, names, animals, and foods — all starting with that letter — before time runs out. It supports multiple languages and is easy to play with people online.

Rocket Goal is a simple 2D physics-based soccer game. Players control a character and try to score goals against an opponent. The controls are easy to learn, but the physics make each match unpredictable and entertaining. It can be played solo against the computer or with a friend on the same device.

Skillwarz is a free-to-play first-person shooter that runs in the browser. It features multiple game modes, different maps, and a variety of weapons. The game focuses on fast-paced combat and rewards players who improve their aim and movement skills over time.

Forward Assault is a tactical first-person shooter with a style similar to Counter-Strike. Two teams — attackers and defenders — compete in short rounds. Players buy weapons before each round and must work together to win. It requires strategy and communication, not just fast reactions.

Slither.io is a browser-based multiplayer game where you control a snake and try to grow as long as possible by eating glowing dots. If your snake's head touches another player, you lose. The goal is to survive and become the biggest snake on the server. Simple rules, but very addictive.
